chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Allah did not appoint a prophet unless He took from him three qualities: Affirming worship as due only to Him, renouncing the rivals (idols set up besides Allah), and that Allah brings forward what He wills and puts back what He wills.

key_terms.يُقَدِّمُ وَيُؤَخِّرُ: Brings forward and puts back (divine decree/Bada')

ai.seo_question: What are the three qualities Allah took from every prophet?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes the universal covenant of prophethood, emphasizing that every prophet affirmed their created status ('abd) and absolute submission to divine will. In Shia theology, this underscores the concept of Bada' (divine changeability in decree) as an attribute of God's wisdom, where He may bring forward or delay what He wills, distinct from human agency. It serves as a foundational proof for the infallible prophets' complete reliance on Allah's sovereign decision-making.
